facts.text: Hendon’s first proper fire station opened in 1914, a design by architect A that marked the town’s commitment to public safety.
The Midland Main Line reached Hendon in 1868, and the Underground followed in 1923 with Hendon Central station on the Edgware Branch.
In 1925 Duple Coachbuilders opened a factory in Hendon that employed 800 workers, becoming one of the town’s largest employers until its closure in 1970.
A Roman settlement once stood in Hendon, and the Edgware Road was part of the ancient Roman road known as Watling Street.
Historically, Hendon was a civil parish in the hundred of Gore within the county of Middlesex before becoming part of London.
Next to the town hall, Hendon Library was built in 1929 to designs by architect T, serving as a cultural hub for residents.
